Step-Independent Windowing vs Episode-Level Training for Multi-Turn Agent RL

In step-independent windowing, a multi-turn agent trajectory is divided into fixed-size non-overlapping windows (w1, w2, ..., w5). Each window is optimized independently with its own advantage estimate (Â_1 through Â_5). This introduces two failure mechanisms:

Mechanism 1 (M1: Information Loss): Context is truncated at window boundaries. Each window only sees local h-step history, losing access to earlier observations. This imposes a constant performance ceiling.

Mechanism 2 (M2: Sign Misattribution): Under group-relative normalization with binary reward, the advantage sign for each window reflects the episode outcome rather than local action quality. In a failed episode, ALL windows receive negative advantage—including windows where the agent took locally correct actions (e.g., w2). This causes cumulative policy degradation.

Episode-level training treats the full trajectory as a single optimization sample. The complete history is available at every step (eliminating M1), and a single advantage Â_episode applies uniformly (eliminating M2). Successful episodes (Pass) get positive advantage (reinforce), failed episodes (Fail) get negative advantage (suppress)—correctly attributing credit at the episode level.
